topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, contextualizes the lecture within the course, and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Genetics, Chance, and Environmental Influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic process shaped by the balance between intrinsic errors, chance, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as an illustrative case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical agents are metabolically processed to create reactive species that induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Initiation-Promotion Paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation and signaling agonists promote tumor outgrowth following initial DNA damage.

topics.label: Host Proliferative State and Life-Stage Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how tissue developmental stages and active proliferation periods influence host susceptibility to carcinogenic transformation.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying Carcinogens and Assessing Carcinogenic Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro methods used to detect carcinogens and weigh the practical risks of exposure.
